topics.title: COP31 ends without central pact
topics.summary: The COP31 climate summit ended without agreement on its central deal after divisions over fossil fuels, finance and carbon-capture language.
topics.discussionPrompt: When a big group cannot agree on the final version, is it better to leave with a partial win or keep talking until everyone can live with it?

topics.title: AI-assisted maths claim gets verification
topics.summary: Two groups verified a mathematician's claim that AI tool Claude helped solve a long-standing mathematics problem, reopening questions about how research credit may evolve.
topics.discussionPrompt: If an AI helps crack a hard problem, should it get a mention like a calculator, a research assistant, or something entirely new?

topics.title: Canada's daily cannabis use rises
topics.summary: A new Canadian study reports that more people now use cannabis daily than drink alcohol daily, highlighting changing habits since legalization.
topics.discussionPrompt: What makes a social habit feel normal: how common it is, where people do it, the rules around it, or how it is talked about?

topics.title: Newfoundland gold mine plans expansion
topics.summary: A gold mine in central Newfoundland has grown into a small community hub and is preparing to expand, bringing fresh attention to the region's resource economy.
topics.discussionPrompt: Would you rather live near a fast-growing work town with lots of change, or a smaller place that stays familiar year after year?

topics.title: Live cattle auctions keep their place
topics.summary: Alberta ranchers say in-person cattle auctions still matter even as online bidding grows, because buyers and sellers value the atmosphere and direct comparison.
topics.discussionPrompt: For something important, do you trust an online listing, an in-person look, or a recommendation from someone who knows the field?

topics.title: Rental costs outpace home buying
topics.summary: A new report says rents in Britain are expected to rise about twice as quickly as buying costs as a shortage of available homes continues.
topics.discussionPrompt: If you could redesign one part of finding a place to live, would you change prices, location, size, or how people search?

topics.title: School crossing patrols face shortages
topics.summary: Councils in Britain are struggling to recruit enough school crossing patrols, raising concern about keeping familiar routes safe for children.
topics.discussionPrompt: What small neighborhood job seems easy to overlook until it disappears and suddenly everyone notices?

topics.title: Falklands oil plans raise wildlife worries
topics.summary: Proposed oil development around the Falkland Islands is drawing concern from environmental groups focused on seals, whales and penguins in the surrounding waters.
topics.discussionPrompt: When a place has both jobs and remarkable wildlife at stake, what would a fair local decision-making process look like?

topics.title: Dictionary spotlights new tech slang
topics.summary: Macquarie Dictionary named “pervert glasses” its word of the year, ahead of terms including “nudify” and “AI;DR,” reflecting anxiety and humor around new technology.
topics.discussionPrompt: What new word or phrase have you heard lately that perfectly captures a modern problem, even if it sounds a little ridiculous?

topics.title: Miley Cyrus marries Maxx Morando
topics.summary: Miley Cyrus and musician Maxx Morando married in a California ceremony, making entertainment headlines around the world.
topics.discussionPrompt: For a celebration, would you choose a huge party, a tiny gathering, a destination trip, or something wonderfully unexpected?
